item.question: How do robust and stochastic settings differ when dealing with uncertain matrices in StQPs?
item.answer: In a robust setting, decision-makers use an uncertainty set to account for all possible variations within known limits, ensuring no violations occur outside this set. In contrast, a stochastic setting replaces uncertain matrices with their expected values or considers them as random variables following known distributions, allowing for probabilistic handling of uncertainties.
